prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity north-star composition for a native Windows 11 WinUI 3 desktop application
Primary request: Design composition option A for Codex Tweaks using the current Windows 11 Settings application as the quality bar. This is the same native Fluent visual world the user explicitly chose: no custom art direction. Show an app overview screen with a standard left NavigationView, Mica visible in the title/navigation layer, a transparent page, a spacious title area, one prominent connection status surface, and grouped settings surfaces for injection controls, AI authoring, and resource location. Use authentic WinUI proportions, Segoe UI Variable hierarchy, rounded 8px-ish system controls, subtle one-pixel strokes, system accent only for actions, and native InfoBar/ToggleSwitch/Button appearance.
Composition/framing: landscape Windows desktop app window, 1536x1024-like 3:2 viewport, entire first viewport visible. Moderate density and generous whitespace, content aligned to a readable max width.
Text (verbatim, use only these real product strings): “Codex Tweaks”, “概览”, “功能包”, “运行日志”, “关于与更新”, “管理 Codex 的本地界面增强”, “Codex 未运行”, “可以重新打开 Codex”, “打开 Codex”, “控制”, “启用界面增强”, “重新注入”, “交给 AI 编写”, “复制 Skill”, “资源目录”. Other secondary text may be represented by quiet gray lines rather than invented copy.
Color palette: system Windows 11 light theme, Mica pale gray, layered white/near-white content surfaces, user system blue accent, semantic green/amber/red only for status.
Constraints: unmistakably native Windows 11, accessibility-minded contrast, realistic WinUI controls and spacing, no invented metrics or product claims, no non-native icons, no watermark.
Avoid: web dashboard styling, bento grid, nested cards, huge marketing hero, neon terminal, gradients as decoration, glossy glass, custom typography, emoji, fake screenshots of macOS.
